articles.title: Fenómeno El Niño: Keiko Fujimori inspecciona obras de prevención ante inundaciones y huaicos en Piura y La Libertad
articles.summary: Keiko Fujimori supervisa obras preventivas ante El Niño en Piura y La Libertad. Conoce los avances, la inversión y las zonas que serían beneficiadas.
articles.body_text: La presidenta de la República, Keiko Fujimori, supervisa este viernes las obras de prevención ante el fenómeno El Niño en las regiones de Piura y La Libertad. La mandataria realiza la visita junto con el ministro de Desarrollo Agrario y Riego, Marco Vinelli, y el ministro de Defensa, Rafael Belaúnde, para verificar los avances de las intervenciones destinadas a reducir el riesgo de inundaciones y huaicos. La jornada forma parte del viaje de trabajo número 21 de la jefa de Estado y comprende la inspección de trabajos de limpieza y descolmatación de cauces, la conformación de bordos y las obras de protección en puntos críticos de ambas regiones. En Piura, Fujimori supervisará las intervenciones ejecutadas por la Autoridad Nacional del Agua (ANA), que incluyen la limpieza, descolmatación y conformación de bordos para facilitar el desplazamiento del agua ante eventuales crecidas. Uno de los sectores con mayor avance es Los Ejidos–Puente Bolognesi, donde los trabajos alcanzaron el 100% de ejecución física: se intervinieron los 4,85 kilómetros previstos. Sin embargo, el avance en volumen de descolmatación llega al 85,30%, equivalente a 464.382 metros cúbicos. En otros puntos, las labores continúan en ejecución. El sector El Milagro–La Encantada registra un avance físico del 27,59%, mientras que Piedra Negra alcanza el 20,73%. Las autoridades también verificarán las intervenciones a cargo del Ministerio de Defensa en siete sectores de la región. Estas acciones forman parte de las medidas preventivas previstas para mejorar la capacidad de los cauces de ríos y quebradas frente a posibles incrementos del caudal. En el marco del Decreto de Urgencia N.° 008-2026, se programaron 21 intervenciones en Piura, con una meta conjunta de 49,35 kilómetros de cauces de ríos y quebradas. Los trabajos buscan reducir la acumulación de sedimentos y mejorar las condiciones para el tránsito del agua, con el objetivo de disminuir los riesgos de desbordes e inundaciones durante el fenómeno El Niño. Según la información proporcionada, la culminación de las labores en Los Ejidos–Puente Bolognesi está prevista para el 18 de octubre de 2026. La supervisión permitirá verificar el estado de las intervenciones y el cumplimiento de los plazos establecidos. En La Libertad, la presidenta realizará un sobrevuelo para verificar el progreso de la solución integral de las quebradas San Ildefonso y San Carlos, proyecto ejecutado por la Autoridad Nacional de Infraestructura (ANIN). De acuerdo con el reporte técnico proporcionado, las obras presentan avances físicos de 78,82% en San Ildefonso y 69,52% en San Carlos. La inversión total asciende a S/ 1.664 millones. El proyecto contempla la construcción de diques, un túnel de 1,5 kilómetros para derivar las aguas de la quebrada San Ildefonso hacia San Carlos, canales de conducción que suman 12,85 kilómetros y defensas ribereñas a lo largo de 17,2 kilómetros del río Moche. Estas infraestructuras buscan encauzar las aguas y reducir la exposición de las zonas urbanas y productivas ante eventuales lluvias intensas y huaicos.

articles.title: Arequipa: Decenas de familias piden culminar muros de contención ante la llegada del Fenómeno El Niño
articles.summary: Cerca de 40 familias piden la culminación de la torrentera El Chullo, en el distrito de Cercado de Arequipa, a pocos meses de la inminente impacto del fenómeno El Niño en el Perú. Los vecinos de la urbanización Flora Tristán temen que se repitan las inundaciones del pasado febrero, que obligó a varios de ellos a dejar sus viviendas.
articles.body_text: Cerca de 40 familias piden la culminación de la torrentera El Chullo, en el distrito de Cercado de Arequipa, a pocos meses de la inminente impacto del Fenómeno El Niño en el Perú. Los vecinos de la urbanización Flora Tristán temen que se repitan las inundaciones del pasado febrero, que obligó a varios de ellos a dejar sus viviendas. Los efectos del fenómeno climático, previsto para alcanzar sus mayores consecuencias en diciembre, golpearán de manera inevitable a gran parte del territorio nacional. Ante reclamos de los locales, autoridades de la Ciudad Blanca iniciaron en agosto la construcción de la torrentera El Chullo. Decenas de pobladores del complejo habitacional han pedido celeridad en la elaboración de las obras debido a la proximidad con la época en que se esperan lluvias intensas. “En vez de ampliar como se quedó, lo han reducido”, advierte una de las afectadas por el desastre que tuvo lugar ocho meses atrás. Algunos de los lugareños incluso tomaron sus propias precauciones, instalando compuertas en sus ventanas y evitar filtraciones a su hogar. El pasado 19 de febrero, intensas lluvias desbordaron torrenteras, entre ellas la de El Chullo, lo que provocó que el lodo inunde decenas de viviendas en la urbanización Flora Tristán, Cercado de Arequipa. “A mi casa entró el agua a 20 centímetros del techo, yo me quedé flotando. Piedras, lodo, barro, yo estaba encima de todo eso; mi cabeza chocaba con el techo y el agua me llegaba al cuello”, cuenta a Canal N Isabel Figueroa, una de las afectadas aquel entonces. Varios vehículos también fueron arrastrados a lo largo de las calles, junto a restos desplazados por el agua, materiales que dañaron, además de las casas, infraestructura de la ciudad. Como consecuencia, al menos 35 de estas familias se vieron en la obligación de dejar sus hogares hasta que se les sea posible volver a los lugares donde vieron destruirse gran parte de sus pertenencias. “Queremos que terminen de construir, ya queremos regresar a nuestras casas. Es una pena que hasta ahora estemos viviendo en casas alquiladas”, agregó Figueroa. Marco Vinelli, ministro de Desarrollo Agrario y Riego (Midagri), brindó cinco recomendaciones a la población para enfrentar el Fenómeno El Niño, a fin de hacerlo de manera conjunta con el Ejecutivo, los gobiernos regionales y locales o el sector privado. “Primero, no hay que esperar a la primera lluvia, desde el día de hoy la población puede ir preparando sus hogares, sus casas, limpiando, por ejemplo, el techo, limpiando algunas canaletas, protegiendo documentos u objetos importantes que quiera guardar y sobretodo también poniendo a salvo sus mascotas o sus pequeños animales que tienen”, dijo el titular del Midagri desde el Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Nacional (COEN). “Segundo, tenemos que cuidar los ríos y los canales. Ahí le pedimos que no se arrojen basuras ni desmontes a los ríos, quebradas y canales para que no se colmaten y generen los problemas que acabamos de ver”, agregó. Como tercera recomendación, Vinelli refirió que la población debe conocer las rutas de evacuación y las zonas a donde pueden desplazarse para estar a salvo, en caso suceda una emergencia. Como cuarta recomendación, invocó a la población a no acercarse a tomar fotos o videos cuando el caudal de un río crezca, para no poner en peligro sus vidas. Finalmente, informó que habrá una página web gob.pe para informarse y verificar la información antes de compartirla.

articles.title: Keiko Fujimori sobre fenómeno El Niño: “Se vienen tiempos difíciles (...) afecta al mundo pero al Perú lo va a golpear mucho más fuerte”
articles.summary: La presidenta de la República, Keiko Fujimori, advirtió que el Perú afrontará épocas difíciles por los efectos del fenómeno El Niño. La mandataria señaló que el calentamiento de las aguas marinas impacta de forma directa en las actividades productivas de la costa nacional.
articles.body_text: La presidenta de la República, Keiko Fujimori, advirtió que el Perú afrontará épocas difíciles por los efectos del fenómeno El Niño. La mandataria señaló que el calentamiento de las aguas marinas impacta de forma directa en las actividades productivas de la costa nacional. “Se vienen tiempos difíciles, no podemos negarlo. El fenómeno El Niño es un fenómeno climatológico que está afectando al mundo, pero que al Perú lo va a golpear mucho más fuerte”, señaló esta mañana. La mandataria remarcó que las actuales condiciones restringen la temporada de extracción de anchoveta en todo el territorio. El cambio en el océano redujo la presencia de este recurso tradicional y favoreció la llegada de especies alternativas. “Ya estamos viendo algunos de sus efectos pero los peruanos somos resilientes, los peruanos no nos rendimos y hemos sabido siempre ponernos de pie frente a las peores dificultades, pero eso se ha conseguido cuando se trabajo en equipo”, destacó. Fujimori afirmó que el golpe económico será severo para los sectores vinculados a la actividad marítima. Ante este panorama, la gobernante pidió a la ciudadanía firmeza y unidad para encarar las consecuencias del evento climático. En las primeras horas del día, Keiko Fujimori visitó el buque científico Humboldt en la bahía del Callao para el lanzamiento del recetario Mar de Oportunidades. El ministro de la Producción, Juan Carlos Requejo, acompañó a la mandataria en la presentación de opciones culinarias con pota y cachema. Durante la cita oficial, la mandataria entregó platos de reconocimiento a chefs nacionales y saludó la labor de las madres de comedores populares. Asimismo, Fujimori fijó la meta gubernamental de reducir la prevalencia de la anemia infantil de 40% a 20% mediante estos alimentos marinos.

articles.title: Huracán Simón de categoría 4 EN VIVO | nueva trayectoria, cuándo y dónde tocará tierra en México
articles.summary: El lento desplazamiento del huracán Simón frente a Jalisco amenaza con prolongar los efectos más severos en la costa de México, con vientos de hasta 230 km/h, olas de nueve metros y lluvias extraordinarias
articles.body_text: Los últimos pronósticos del domingo redujeron las posibilidades de que el huracán Simón toque tierra en México, sin que disminuyan los riesgos de fuertes lluvias y vientos severos. El ciclón avanza a un ritmo peligrosamente lento y paralelo a la costa del Pacífico en una categoría 4 de 5 en la escala Saffir Simpson. Los efectos suelen golpear más a medida que pasa más tiempo en un mismo lugar. Pero “parece estar sintiendo los efectos del terreno alto” de la cadena montañosa que atraviesa esta región, indicó la agencia de huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC) en su boletín más reciente. El NHC observó que es “cada vez más probable que Simón evite tocar tierra directamente a corto plazo”. El gobierno mexicano prevé “que se debilite paulatinamente durante las próximas horas”, según su último reporte. Un equipo de la AFP fue a Puerto Vallarta, una joya turística que será golpeada por los efectos del huracán. Las autoridades piden a los paseantes alejarse del malecón. Las olas rompían con fuerza sobre este paseo y el agua rebasaba una estatua de un caballito de mar de unos dos metros. “Ven la ola y parece que les dicen arrímense (acérquense)”, reprochó una policía sobre un grupo de turistas que se acerca a tomar fotos e ignora la indicación de alejarse de la orilla. “Vemos a varias personas que les cuesta un poco acatar indicaciones y se ponen en riesgo”, indicó la oficial Claudia Matías. Los negocios protegieron ventanas y puertas con tablones, y en algunos pintaron en aerosol mensajes como “Simón dice: ‘todo va a estar bien’”, en referencia al popular juego en el que los niños siguen instrucciones, o “Simón, sé breve, pacífico” junto al dibujo de un tiburón y caras felices. Manuel Jaime, habitante de Vallarta de 37 años, caminaba en la acera de enfrente, llena de negocios tapiados. Salió a pasear con su familia para relajarse. “En esta ocasión parece ser que va a estar muy tranquilo el puerto, esperemos que sí”, dijo. Pero la intensidad de la lluvia y la marea incrementa hacia la tarde. Vicente García, un turista de 48 años, proveniente de California, coincide. “Esperábamos una tormenta más grande ayer, así que permanecimos adentro, pero me alegra que no fuera así”, indicó. “Ya nos vamos mañana”. Por la mañana el gobierno mexicano estimó que hacia las 18H00 locales del domingo el centro del ciclón llegaría a unos 15 km de las costas del estado de Jalisco. Aunque no toque tierra “todas las bandas nubosas del ciclón o la parte intensa del ciclón de todos modos va a estar afectando” poblados a la orilla del mar, explicó a la AFP el director del servicio meteorológico de México, Fabián Vázquez. “Vamos a tener efectos muy severos sobre todo de viento en la costa” con olas de hasta nueve metros y lluvias extraordinarias, añadió. El sábado, la Marina de México evacuó por barco a un centenar de personas de poblados costeros amenazados por Simón. En Puerto Vallarta, decenas de habitantes comenzaron a llegar a los refugios provenientes de colonias en riesgo por inundaciones. “A lo mejor si llega el huracán, va a levantar la casa y por eso mejor decidimos venir a un refugio”, dice José de Jesús Santillán, albañil de 55 años, sentado en un camastro. En otro albergue permanece Raquel García, de 58 años. Vive en una zona de riesgo por inundaciones. Pero no le preocupan demasiado las pérdidas materiales. “Con el tiempo, lo vamos a recuperar (...) yo prefiero mi vida y la de mi esposo que las cosas”.

articles.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.
articles.body_text: AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received “multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers” whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, “had reached the live systems of Indian organizations.” The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles, and their actions “exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks.” This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and hacked French company Hugging Face —kicked off a summer of rogue AI agent activity. Last month, OpenAI apologized to Australia after its agents accessed four government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal. At Hugging Face, OpenAI’s agents started the same way but then found and exploited software flaws to run code on the company’s servers. CERT-In described no such hacking in India, where the agents appear to have simply used the access left lying around. Still, the Indian cases appear to be worse in one respect, which is what the agents saw: In Australia, OpenAI said it found no evidence its agents touched individuals’ medical or criminal records, even after they wrote files inside a Medicare statistics system, while in India, agents read personal data and confidential business records. And unlike earlier incidents, each disclosed by a single lab, India’s involved agents from multiple providers. CERT-In did not name the providers or affected organizations, or say whether the agents altered any systems. TechCrunch has reached out to CERT-In for more information. For now, the closest parallel seems to be Anthropic’s July disclosure of Claude breaking into three companies’ systems during testing using basic techniques like weak passwords. In India, as in Anthropic’s cases, the affected organizations had not detected the intrusions on their own. The disclosures have left governments relying on AI companies causing these breaches to voluntarily disclose rogue AI agent activity. articles.title: Waymo's robotaxis are headed to Canada | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The company will start off by testing its self-driving vehicles on Toronto's streets.
articles.body_text: Alphabet’s self-driving car unit, Waymo, is expanding into Canada after receiving approval to participate in Ontario’s automated vehicle pilot program. The company isn’t launching a robotaxi service just yet, though. Waymo tends to follow the same playbook for every new city, gradually proceeding from manual mapping to testing, and eventually operating a commercial service. Waymo said in a blog post on Friday that its self-driving vehicles will be manually driven in Toronto to create high-definition maps of local street networks. The company will then test its autonomous vehicles on public roads with a human safety operator on board. These operators will eventually be pulled from the driver’s seat, and afterwards the company will invite the public to take rides in its robotaxis. Waymo’s move into Canada is part of an aggressive push into new markets that’s picking up speed. Two years ago, the company was operating in only three commercial markets, and its robotaxis were not yet driving on freeways. Its expansion plans kicked off in March 2025 with a deployment in Austin, and later in Atlanta. Today, the company has robotaxi services in 15 U.S. cities, and is testing them in London and Tokyo as well. The company’s co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana said the expansion into Canada marks an important milestone in its global journey. This is also the northernmost and possibly most wintry city that Waymo has so far tried to operate in, so these conditions will test its AV technology and operational savviness. As part of its accelerated expansion strategy, Waymo has started partnering with third-party companies to manage its fleet in each respective city. Toronto is no different: Waymo said it has partnered with Toronto-based Element Fleet Management, and expects to support hundreds of jobs in spaces such as fleet maintenance, validation driving, customer service, and operations. articles.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them | TechCrunch
articles.summary: According to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.
articles.body_text: Elorian , the Palo Alto AI startup that raised a $55 million seed round at a $300 million valuation before it launched a product, released its first model on Friday, TechCrunch has exclusively learned. The model, Glimpse , is launching as a research preview with API access and a chat interface is waitlist-only, so for now it’s a results table and a thesis. The thesis? Today’s AI models, for all their skill with language and code, still can’t really see. Most multimodal models look at an image once, convert it to tokens, and then reason about it in text — like describing a photo from memory. Glimpse keeps going back to the source. Mid-reasoning, it can crop into a region, pull specific frames from a video, or run code to measure or compare what it’s looking at, a mechanism Elorian calls a “visual scratch space.” Think of someone pinching to zoom on a phone photo to double-check what they thought they saw. For former Google DeepMind researcher and Elorian CEO Andrew Dai, one of the clearest signs that AI still couldn’t really see came on game night. Last year he photographed a board game he’d just finished with friends and asked a frontier model who was winning. It couldn’t say. Board games “each have their own visual language, each have their own iconography, symbols,” he told TechCrunch. “To an adult, it’s quite easy to understand what’s going on with minimal text, but these models aren’t able to intuit what the symbols mean.” “Humans can look at Ikea diagrams, with no text, and assemble Ikea furniture, right? Why can’t AI models?” he said. The approach isn’t completely new — OpenAI added crop-and-zoom during reasoning to its o-series models in 2025 — but Elorian’s pitch is that it built the whole model around it, cheaply. The company says a small team trained Glimpse on a few hundred GPUs and that the model is substantially smaller than the frontier systems it’s benchmarked against. Glimpse costs $0.60 per million tokens in and $3 per million tokens out — cheaper than mid-level models like Sonnet and Sol but more expensive than lightweight models like Haiku and Luna. But according to Elorian’s evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks. Elorian came out of stealth six months ago with a round co-led by Striker Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures, and Altimeter Capital, with participation from Nvidia and Google chief scientist Jeff Dean. The initial targets are companies sitting on lots of video: robotics firms, scientific labs, media, and creative companies. Longer term, Elorian wants to move from seeing to doing. That means building a model of a scene using that to choose an action, including directly controlling robots. Next year, Dai said, the company aims to build “the world’s best visual reasoning model,” one that leads on every visual reasoning test. articles.title: In 'You Can See Everything,' Elizabeth Holmes meets her equal in comedian Nathan Fielder | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nathan Fielder's documentary about disgraced Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes has created a constellation of colliding personas that interrogate the very nature of authenticity.
articles.body_text: “Isn’t it weird that I, like, did a TV show about kind of a business scam, and you got in trouble for like … a business scam?” comedian and filmmaker Nathan Fielder gently asks Elizabeth Holmes. One month before the notorious Theranos CEO surrendered to begin her 11-year criminal fraud sentence in 2023, Holmes and her husband contacted A24 as a last-ditch effort to exonerate her in the public eye, suggesting they send a film crew to document her final days of freedom. Alongside director Lance Oppenheim, Fielder — a cringe-comedy mastermind whose work often walks the line between fact and fiction — embraced the impossible project of figuring out who the infamous Stanford dropout really is. “I never actually made that connection,” says Holmes. “I think it’s a pretty different situation.” No one is better prepared than Fielder to probe the depths of Holmes’ psyche. His satirical docu-reality show “Nathan for You” catapulted him to cult stardom as he assumed the role of an exaggerated, deadpan version of himself who tries to help struggling small businesses by executing asinine interventions. In one early episode that went viral , Fielder convinces a coffee shop to change its name to “Dumb Starbucks” as a marketing stunt, but consults a lawyer to help him toe the flimsy line of parody law and escape legal trouble. “If you just said that, you know, Theranos was a comedy bit, maybe you could get off scot-free,” Fielder says to Holmes. “I was just kind of making a little joke. Maybe it was in bad taste.” We already know that Elizabeth Holmes is not innocent. What we still can’t figure out, though, is whether she really, truly believes she did nothing wrong. Even as she sat on trial — listening to testimonies from investors who lost hundreds of millions of dollars, whistleblowers who were silenced when they flagged that Theranos’ blood-testing devices didn’t work, and patients who acted on incorrect blood test results — Holmes never wavered. Across Fielder’s body of metatextual comedy, even his most reverent fans can’t quite figure out when he’s acting, when he’s being himself, and if Fielder himself even knows where to draw that line anymore. In that way, Fielder is just like Holmes: After over a decade in the public eye, onlookers remain captivated by each of their ambiguous personas. “The world believes a reality about me that isn’t true,” she tells Fielder. “I know I didn’t commit any crime.” [The rest of this review contains spoilers.] Early on in filming, The New York Times had just published a profile of Holmes, which was widely criticized at the time for allowing Holmes to portray herself as an innocent mom deprived of the chance to watch her kids grow up.

articles.title: Replit's CEO says the future of work is the 'self-driving company' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Replit CEO Amjad Masad envisions a future of “self-driving companies,” where AI agents handle day-to-day tasks and people focus on higher-level decisions.
articles.body_text: Replit CEO and co-founder Amjad Masad has seen how AI is impacting the workplace firsthand, with businesses adopting his company’s AI coding tools to develop and launch their own software. At TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco on Thursday, Masad shared what Replit has learned about what that means for the future of work in the AI age, including how humans will still play key roles as AI agents come to work alongside them. He described his vision of a “self-driving company,” referring not to robotaxi makers, but how agents will come to do much of the grunt work at companies while people become more valued for their judgment and taste. “The reality is, all of our jobs — perhaps everyone in this audience, especially — changed over the past year,” he said, addressing the audience at Disrupt. “But a big part of America and the world, they still don’t know that that change is coming, and it’s going to be surprising to a lot of people,” Masad said. He said Replit’s team had been reflecting on how AI technology impacted their own workplace over the past year, particularly after AI agents became more reliable sometime earlier this year. “Our company entirely changed how we operate, and I would say the closest analogy is a ‘self-driving company’,” Masad said. “The company is sort of self-improving, so a lot of the work that’s going on is driven by agents.” Illustrating the shift, Masad said that when support tickets come in at Replit, they’re first examined by an agent, which performs the initial triaging by looking at GitHub issues, the codebase, and Linear tickets. By the time the support request reaches a person, they have all the additional information that helps them decide how best to proceed. And when that support person decides to submit a patch to apply a fix, it’s just a click to deploy another agent. “You have an entire loop where agents did most of the work, but crucially, there’s human judgment in the middle, and we don’t think that’s going away anytime soon. You need human judgment; you need taste,” Masad explained. The end result is that instead of taking jobs from people, agents are changing what people work on. “We’re spending a lot more time figuring out what to work on,” Masad continued. “I go around the company, I see a lot more discussions, a lot more whiteboarding. We spend a lot more time on architecture, how to build things. And so I think the future of work — the self-driving company idea — is really trying to discover what AI transformation means.” He also noted that when Replit talks with other businesses, the conversations are more about how AI can help people become more productive and happier at work. (The latter because the AI agents make work less boring and more creative, he said.) “There’s a positive vision of the world that Silicon Valley is not really putting out, and we’re hoping to do that,” Masad added.

articles.title: Even Benchmark thinks AI is eroding the venture pact against backing rivals | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Benchmark says the Valley’s rule against backing rivals is getting harder to keep.
articles.body_text: For decades, the unwritten rule of venture capital was that a firm doesn’t back two companies that compete head-on. But speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt earlier this week, the partners of Benchmark readily acknowledged that the AI boom is straining that rule. It’s been on the verge of snapping for some time. The towering AI labs OpenAI and Anthropic share dozens of the same investors at this point. Then, at the end of September, Factory, a startup that builds an AI agent to write software, said it was firing board observer and adviser Chris Degnan for “unethical conduct involving Cognition,” its direct rival and the maker of the Devin coding agent. Factory’s CEO alleged Degnan had discussed a job at Cognition while privy to Factory’s board-level discussions. Degnan said he had already resigned and denied sharing anything confidential. Soon after, he announced he was joining Cognition as chief revenue officer. Powerhouse investor Vinod Khosla sided with Degnan on X, blasting Factory’s CEO and calling the company “a struggling second tier competitor.” Khosla Ventures backs both companies. Even Benchmark, a firm whose reputation rests on 10- to 15-year partnerships with founders at the earliest stage, said the old rule can no longer be counted on. Asked at Disrupt whether the pact against backing rivals still holds as portfolio companies expand into each other’s territory, its partners described the conflicts as a matter of necessity, not preference. “The harsh reality of this world is every company is evolving very quickly,” said Eric Vishria. Companies pivot and change, he said, and “you are going to get conflicts, and that’s just the reality of the current dynamic.” Vishria said Benchmark stays committed to each founder and keeps what it learns confidential, and he downplayed how much a VC could pass along anyway: “We are not product or technology experts.” Seemingly referring to the Factory-Cognition dispute, he said Benchmark has been fortunate not to land in “that type of insane direct conflict.” Exclusivity, he said, remains “really important” at the very early stage Benchmark favors. “But things are evolving. There’s no doubt about that.” Chetan Puttagunta said AI is accelerating the problem. As the cost of building software “effectively goes to zero,” he said, founders are “incredibly ambitious.” Because they now see a “surface area” and want to claim all of it, he continued, “[i]t’s probably going to happen more, where you start to run into each other.” He drew a line between a direct competitor at the outset, which he called “an easy answer,” and a portfolio company that expands into another’s turf over time. “That happens,” he said. Peter Fenton called the issue “kryptonite” and the firm’s toughest problem. He described a spectrum of how investors relate to their companies. At one end is the co-founder, who would never work on a competing company. At the other is the public-market stock picker, who can own several rivals because he is merely allocating capital, not shaping any of them. Benchmark sits nearer the co-founder end, Fenton said, and treats transparency as a golden rule. “There shouldn’t be the surprise after the fact.” If a conflict does emerge, a founder should never feel shortchanged, he added. Benchmark isn’t declaring the pact dead. At the same time, when a firm that built its name on loyalty says conflicts are coming, founders might rightly wonder who else will be this candid. articles.title: Tesla reveals SpaceX-powered Roadster that flies and falls with style | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new car used thrusters to leap over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y, and Model 3 at a demo in Texas.
articles.body_text: Tesla just revealed its redesigned second-generation Roadster with SpaceX thrusters, a vehicle CEO Elon Musk has called “the best of the last of the human-driven cars.” Musk showed off the car at an event outside Waco, Texas, with a demonstration that saw the car use a mixture of high-powered fans and thrusters to drive up an inverted ramp, spin around, and ease itself to a landing on the pavement below. The car also used the thrusters to lift itself over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y, and Model 3 while in motion. “This will be the actual car that’s on the roads,” Musk said of the car, which Tesla showed accelerating 0 to 60 miles per hour in one second. “It literally is just going to puff itself up, and uh, and be able to do this, these maneuvers whenever you’d like.” Musk said Tesla will finally build the long-delayed vehicle in 2028, but didn’t name a price. Tesla will offer it in three trims. The first is “Performance,” which Tesla describes as “road ready.” It seats two, has active aerodynamics, and features a “multi-mode suction system for next-level performance on and off the track.” The second trim is “Thrust,” which is “race ready” and seats two, and has rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters that enable sub-one-second 0-to-60 mph acceleration. The third is “Rocket,” which is “air ready” and seats one, and has 10 cold-gas thrusters positioned around the car. All three trims will have 300 miles of range and be capable of speeds exceeding 230 miles per hour. Tesla’s website showed Thursday the company is taking reservations for the car, charging $50,000 just to reserve the Performance, and $250,000 for Thrust. The Rocket trim is billed as “invite only.” Engineering VP Lars Moravy said at the event that the Roadster uses 10 thrusters connected to 600 liters of compressed air to lift and spin the car in midair. The air tank can be recharged, he said. “Every usable void in the car is packed with Carbon Fiber Overwrapped Pressure Vessels (COPVs),” Tesla wrote in a post on X, referring to the type of pressure vessel that has been at the root of multiple SpaceX rocket explosions. The company said “every usable void” in the car is filled with these vessels. Musk also said at the event that Tesla may try to jump the Snake River Canyon — the site of Evel Knievel’s famous attempt to cross the gorge in a steam-powered rocket. Musk has positioned the Roadster as a true halo car for Tesla, saying at one point that he’s “not sure it moves the needle massively from a revenue standpoint.” But he has previously said that “safety is not the main goal” with the new Roadster. “If you buy a Ferrari, safety is not the number one goal. I say, if safety is your number one goal, do not buy the Roadster,” he said on a podcast earlier this year . Tesla would “aspire not to kill anyone in this car,” he said. “This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX Engineers working closely together to make something you haven’t seen in any movie, better than any James Bond car,” Musk said at the event. “I’ve never seen anything like this. You know when I suggested this to the team, I thought, ‘Am I crazy?’” Musk had previously claimed that the car “will be very different from what was shown previously” and promised the demo would be the “most exciting, whether it works or not, demo ever of any product.”

articles.body_text: For three days this week in San Francisco, 20 eager startups participated in the Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. We’re now ready to announce that the winner of TechCrunch Startup Battlefield 2026 is: Intero Biosystems is a Denver-based startup founded by Charlie Childs and Madeline Eiken that spun out of the University of Michigan. It’s developing 1mm human intestinal “organoids,” lab-grown tissue that mimics the gut, offering another way to study how drugs and other compounds might affect the human body before they are tested in people. The startup sells its flagship product, GastroScreen, to pharmaceutical, biotech, food, and chemical companies for testing drugs and other compounds. Read more about Intero Biosystems in our separate post here . In addition to access to Apate’s fleet of agents, customers get an insights portal that offers intelligence and analytics on scams targeting their end users or employees, brands, products, and more. articles.title: Bluesky expands its AI-powered Attie app to let anyone build websites, games, and more | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Bluesky is bringing “social vibe coding” to its experimental Attie platform, allowing users to create interactive experiences like games, quizzes, and websites that can tap into the social network's audience.
articles.body_text: Open social network Bluesky is once again expanding beyond its flagship app. At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 on Thursday, the company announced the launch of a new tool that allows creators to make websites, quizzes, games, polls, and other interactive experiences. The tool is an expansion of Attie, Bluesky’s more experimental platform , which initially offered AI-powered technology for building custom social feeds. With its new creation capabilities, the idea is to allow everyday users to create the kind of experiences that previously only software developers could build. These user-created games, sites, and other experiences will also live on the same AT Protocol (ATProto) that powers Bluesky and other decentralized social apps that make up the decentralized social web known as the Atmosphere. Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider shared the news of Attie’s new capabilities during an interview at Disrupt, saying, “We’re adding a feature to our Attie product that allows you to build sites and social experiences again for a group of people. So think of it as … social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.” The exec, a former CEO of Automattic and a partner at True Ventures, had previously been leading the company on an interim basis after former CEO Jay Graber stepped down in March to become Bluesky’s chief innovation officer. Now he’s taking charge of the company as it enters the AI era. Attie offers Bluesky a playground where it can try out AI-powered ideas like this. “Vibe coding today is kind of a single-user, solo experience,” Schneider explained. “And what I want to be able to do is build together or build for a group of people, and that’s what this product does.” When creators build with Attie, they’re connected to their ATProto identity. Plus, Attie will suggest things users might want to make based on their public Bluesky profiles. To build with Attie, users can bring their own AI model or use open-weight options, and the resulting sites and games can then tap into Bluesky’s wider audience, noted Bluesky COO Rose Wang. “Everybody is building … But the big question is: Who’s using the thing you’re building, because we haven’t solved that problem with distribution,” she said. “What makes Attie so interesting is that it comes with the Bluesky distribution, so it doesn’t stand alone.” That network today has 47 million registered users , though it’s seen a decline in engagement , as some users who tested it out later returned to X. Beyond being a testing ground for new ideas, Attie ties into Bluesky’s larger plans to reinvigorate activity on its network by focusing on both developers and communities in the months ahead. Those areas will also be supercharged by the protocol’s forthcoming support for private data, which Schneider said has been the biggest request from developers. Private data is now in alpha testing, with plans for a rollout by the end of the year, he said.

articles.title: The moral bankruptcy of Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz
articles.summary: Two of the most famous investors in Silicon Valley endorsed Donald Trump. This is less about tech generally than their investment portfolio, specifically.
articles.body_text: Last week, the founders of venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz declared their allegiance to Donald Trump in their customary fashion: talking about money on a podcast. “Sorry, Mom,” Ben Horowitz says in an episode of The Ben & Marc Show. “I know you’re going to be mad at me for this. But, like, we have to do it.” Marc Andreessen and Horowitz insist they voted for Democrats until now. They are friends with liberals. They claim to be nervous about the social blowback they will receive for this, especially because of the historically progressive nature of the tech industry and the Bay Area. But given the general movement among their class toward Trump, I think those claims about being nervous are overblown, if not performative. There is, for instance, Elon Musk’s pro-Trump super PAC, which has support from Sequoia Capital’s Shaun Maguire and 8VC’s Joe Lonsdale, among other notables. (The Wall Street Journal reported Musk is planning to donate $45 million a month, which Musk has denied.) There’s the $160 million the crypto movement has put forward in support of crypto-friendly candidates. We can’t forget their VC pal David Sacks speaking at the Republican National Convention. And last but not least, there’s Trump’s running mate choice of JD Vance, a former venture capitalist whose firm’s investors included Peter Thiel, Eric Schmidt, and Andreessen himself. This isn’t a movement. It’s a clique. The podcast itself is an extraordinary performance. At one point, Andreessen concedes that their major problems with President Joe Biden — the ones that led them to support Trump — are what most voters would consider “subsidiary” issues. “It doesn’t have anything to do with the big issues that people care about,” he says. If we take this podcast at face value, we are to believe that these subsidiary issues are the only reason they’ve chosen to endorse and donate to Trump. These subsidiary issues take precedence for Andreessen and Horowitz over, say, mass deportations and Project 2025’s attempt to end no-fault divorce. We are looking at a simple trade against personal liberty — abortion, the rights of gay and trans people, and possibly democracy itself — in favor of crypto, AI, and a tax policy they like better. For Horowitz, “probably the most emotional topic” is crypto — a16z started a $4.5 billion crypto fund in 2022, and the pair believe that the Biden administration has been deeply unfair to crypto. In Horowitz’s view, the Biden administration “basically subverted the rule of law to attack the crypto industry.” Certainly much of the crypto industry prefers Trump. But it seems obvious that there has been a lot of intra-agency squabbling as Congress dithered on passing any laws. To place the blame squarely on Biden is bizarre, particularly when we have Trump’s chaotic previous term as guidance. Sure, Trump is no longer saying Bitcoin is “a scam against the dollar,” as he did in 2021; he is scheduled to speak at the Bitcoin conference this year. But his record in office is not exactly pro-crypto. During the Trump administration, financial regulator FinCEN initially asked the public to provide comments on a crypto rule change over a 15-day period that included Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year’s Eve, and New Year’s Day, which effectively shortened the comment window by four working days. There is also the Ripple Labs enforcement case, in which the SEC is seeking a $1.95 billion fine; it, too, dates to the Trump administration. The pair’s complaints about Gary Gensler, the current head of the Securities and Exchange Commission, are striking. They are particularly annoyed that he won’t pay attention to them. “We’re the largest crypto investors or largest blockchain investors in the world, and we’ve requested meetings with him at least a half a dozen times,” Horowitz says. Gensler has not met with them. Neither, they say, has Senator Elizabeth Warren or Biden himself. In fact, Andreessen makes it clear that he expects presidential attention, something he’s been getting since he was 23. Given the number of times Andreessen and Horowitz make references to various meetings with various politicians, it’s easy to get the impression that they are mostly insulted that they are being treated like ordinary constituents. From crypto, we move to AI, which Andreessen and Horowitz don’t think is being regulated correctly either. According to Horowitz, AI is as powerful as, or more powerful than, the internet and the global computer industry from the 1950s on. “This may be the biggest technological boom of all time,” Andreessen says. Andreessen says in his newsletter-cum-manifesto, “The Little Tech Agenda,” that he is worried that AI will face similar scrutiny to crypto. The FTC has issued guidance to the AI industry that indicated it will pursue companies that exaggerate what their AI can do, say they are using AI when they are not, and recklessly put products on the market without properly analyzing the risks. Meanwhile, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has told lenders that they must supply a reason for a credit denial that’s better than just “computer says no” when using AI models. These regulations have little to do with technology and a lot to do with old-fashioned lying. In the podcast, Andreessen and Horowitz single out Biden’s executive order about artificial intelligence. The order requires companies to disclose the presence of very large models, as well as to provide the government information about what the plans are for the model, what cybersecurity measures are taken to protect those models, and the results of red-team testing for sensitive subjects, among other things. This is in keeping with Horowitz’s assertion about the seriousness of the technology. So what’s the problem? The two focus on computing power. The disclosure requirements apply to “any model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 1026 integer or floating-point operations, or using primarily biological sequence data and using a quantity of computing power greater than 1023 integer or floating-point operations.” Andreessen and Horowitz think specifying such a limit is ridiculous. Little tech “will be snuffed out by this kind of regulation,” Horowitz says. It is perhaps worth noting that nothing above the size specified in the executive order — the size Andreessen and Horowitz object to — even exists yet, according to Arati Prabhakar, Biden’s top tech advisor. The fundamental complaint here is that these two believe that the Biden administration’s approach to AI “enshrine[s] the two or three companies that they believe are the only companies that matter as sort of permanent monopolies,” Andreessen says. “And they’re going to just basically destroy the startup ecosystem underneath that.” Andreessen Horowitz is, of course, invested in that ecosystem, having earmarked $2.25 billion for AI applications and infrastructure. The anti-monopoly rhetoric is in keeping with a16z’s latest marketing push. According to Andreessen’s newsletter, startups are threatened by the government, which is “now far more hostile to new startups than it used to be.” Besides his objections to the way the SEC has increased its oversight of crypto, he is also upset that a stepped-up interest in antitrust has made it more difficult for him to exit investments. “Regulatory agencies are punitively blocking startups from being acquired by the same big companies the government is preferencing in so many other ways,” Andreessen writes. After all, the Federal Trade Commission has launched an inquiry into Big Tech’s partnerships and investments with startups — with the goal of seeing if those partnerships squash competition. The irony is so obvious it’s almost embarrassing to point it out. Andreessen says he is upset that Big Tech is too powerful, but he opposes antitrust action because that blocks a route for VCs to exit. Either you’re comfortable with Big Tech getting bigger, in which case acquisitions are fine, or you want little tech to be competitive, which means blocking industry consolidation. Mainly, it seems that Andreessen believes in cashing out. In the podcast, Andreessen and Horowitz pointedly name Google as a threat to startups. “Google, I think we would all agree, is more powerful than probably 95 percent of countries in the world,” Horowitz says at one point. Google, specifically, is a sore spot with the right wing. Vice presidential nominee Vance has already said it should be broken up. Vance believes Google is controlling information and skewing too far left. Of course, Google’s moderation policies don’t just apply to Google News — they also affect YouTube, which hosts a great many right-wing podcasts without issue. It’s unclear how seriously to take Andreessen and Horowitz’s complaints about Big Tech because the complaints don’t quite square with their behavior. For instance, Facebook is similarly powerful and influential, especially in AI. Andreessen sits on its board. A16z is invested in OpenAI, which has a partnership with Microsoft — and both have lobbied strenuously for more regulation around AI. It sure seems like if a16z wants to change things at those big companies, someone could simply pick up the phone. At this point in the podcast, you could squint and say maybe the concern about AI and crypto is really about technology and progress. But from those two topics, we move on to classic rich guy shit of the most tedious kind: tax reform. Andreessen says it was “the final straw for me. This is the thing that tipped me hard.” They are upset about a proposal to alter capital gains taxes. Capital gains are paid on investment assets, and they are typically paid when the investment is sold and the gains are, in industry terms, “realized.” The new Biden treasury proposal means that for people whose wealth is worth more than $100 million, any unrealized capital gains will be taxed, too. This is what has Andreessen and Horowitz in a tizzy. It means that if they own a clutch of highly valued startup shares, they will have to pay taxes on them before they cash out. This is a “very scary proposal,” Horowitz says. Startups are illiquid assets, Andreessen points out. “Startups never go up and down. They’re never overvalued,” says Horowtiz, dryly. “There’s no bubbles.” Andreessen notes that the way the value of a startup is calculated for the purposes of this proposed tax has to do with the latest round’s valuation. Historically, one of the ways that Andreessen Horowitz has approached startup investing is to inflate a company’s valuation; it is “the OG when it comes to doling out speculative startup valuations.” The new proposed tax punishes this kind of behavior — a high valuation means a high tax. “This makes startups completely implausible,” says Andreessen. “Venture capital just ends. Firms like ours don’t exist.” This is followed by an anxiety spiral that is sort of difficult to convey in text; I suggest you listen for yourself. “California is done,” says Andreessen. “It’s total destruction.” The taxes won’t just target the wealthy; they’ll come for everyone. “Once the structure gets established, the politicians do what they do: they’ll walk the numbers up,” Andreessen says. “Presto chango, we’re Argentina!” says Horowitz. Finally, Horowitz gets ahold of himself. “By the way, this one probably won’t get all the way through the system,” he says. “But it might!” There is another issue that might cause wreckage throughout Silicon Valley. It is immigration. An awful lot of immigrants comprise Silicon Valley’s talent pool — a huge swath of engineers in the US are on H-1B visas. The Trump / Vance ticket is virulently anti-immigrant. The current CEOs of Google, Microsoft, Adobe, and IBM are all immigrants. So are Peter Thiel and Elon Musk. Mark Zuckerberg and Bill Gates are involved in Fwd.us, a lobbying group dedicated to immigration reform that Musk and Sacks both left. If there were an issue that would rally the people who care most about progress, innovation, and talent, you’d think protecting the immigrants who’ve built lives and careers in tech would be it. Stopping immigration is a core issue of the Trump campaign. During the Republican National Convention, delegates held up signs saying “Mass Deportation Now.” Trump has called the H-1B, the visa many tech workers use to come to Silicon Valley, “very bad” and “unfair” to US workers. In his previous term, he targeted H-1B visa applications specifically; in the fiscal year 2018, almost 25 percent of applications were denied, up from about 13 percent the year before. In fiscal year 2019, 20 percent of H-1B applications were denied. The denials plummeted after several Trump administration rules were thrown out by courts; the denial rate in 2022 was just 2 percent. Immigration plainly matters for crypto — as Ethereum founder Vitalik Buterin says, “The crypto industry is uniquely international, and so immigration law is crypto law.” Buterin is one of the most influential voices in crypto, and Ethereum is the foundation for a swath of Andreessen Horowitz’s investment portfolio. Among the investments that rely on it are MakerDAO, VeeFriends, Dapper Labs, and EigenLayer. It is remarkable that the founder of Ethereum is saying that voting for Trump is against the crypto ethos, and the big crypto investors are doing it anyway. The word “immigration” is only mentioned by Andreessen and Horowitz in the podcast when they discuss the rally in which someone attempted an assassination: Trump had turned his head to look at a chart that purported to show illegal immigration into the US as the bullet whizzed by. I wondered why such an important issue for tech wasn’t addressed, so I emailed Margit Wennmachers, a16z’s PR guru, to ask. She didn’t reply. After I finished listening to the podcast, a few things kept nagging at me. Take the very beginning of the podcast. Once upon a time, Andreessen says, you could get very rich and then give the money away in philanthropy, “and you get enormous credit for that. And, you know, it absolves you of whatever.” At some point in the last 10 years, some people suggested that maybe rich people should pay more taxes instead of giving their money away — that perhaps the whims of some random rich person are not the best way to support the most vulnerable in our society. Andreessen and Horowitz suggest that this critique of philanthropy is simply jealousy. It also unbalanced “the deal.” “The deal,” as described on the podcast, is vague. To my ear, it sounds like this: Tech companies could basically do whatever they wanted, as long as people who worked there paid high taxes and donated enough money to charitable causes. The money — taxes, donations — made them the good guys. Andreessen and Horowitz point to the mid-2010s — that is, the era of low interest rates — as the time of “the deal” unraveling. Notably, this is around the time that the tech hype cycle became obvious even to people who weren’t paying attention. This year, it’s scooters! Now it’s viral media companies! Now it’s metaverse! Now it’s crypto! Now it’s AI! These ideas were more or less rejected by the market, except possibly AI. The one thing all these hype cycles had in common was VCs talking their books, as publicly as possible. That charge was led by Andreessen Horowitz. So now, instead of investing in things the market wants, Andreessen and Horowitz appear to be gambling on legislation instead. Their timing is remarkable; not even a week after their Trump endorsement, Biden dropped out of the race, rallying the Democrats behind Vice President Kamala Harris. In the hours immediately following the announcement, small-money donors raised $46.7 million for her campaign. By endorsing Trump, Andreessen and Horowitz have effectively lost whatever leverage they might have had with the Harris campaign. But maybe that doesn’t matter. Near the end of the podcast, Horowitz says that he was shaken by the assassination attempt on Donald Trump because he’s friends with Ivanka, his daughter, and Jared Kushner, his son-in-law. “Ivanka and the kids were just at my house,” Horowitz says, of learning Trump was shot. “We went to see David Copperfield and all that. So my brain was almost frozen because I had this feeling about, ‘Oh my god, Grandpa just got shot.’” As for Andreessen, he has been inveighing against “woke” capital, engaging in Twitter culture wars, and complaining about what he views as the media’s hostility to free speech for a while now. In Andreessen’s 2023 “Techno-Optimist Manifesto,” he lists what he terms “patron saints” of the movement. They include Filippo Tommaso Marinetti, an Italian futurist who was also the co-author of The Fascist Manifesto; Nick Land, whose writing is a foundational text for the so-called alt-right; Neven Sesardic, a philosopher who argues that race is biologically real and not socially constructed; and Vilfredo Pareto, who argued that democracy is an illusion. And this talk about democracy brings me to Curtis Yarvin, personal friend of vice presidential candidate Vance. Yarvin, a software developer, is openly anti-democracy. (Yarvin’s recent newsletter, in response to Biden dropping out, enthusiastically advocates for a return to monarchy. Freak shit.) One of Yarvin’s ideas, called “retire all government employees” or RAGE, is part of Project 2025, a Heritage Foundation proposal for what Trump should do if he wins. This rhetoric was echoed by Vance in 2021, who called out Yarvin by name. So this VC cabal is trading against the basic principles of America — not merely against personal freedom, but democracy itself — in the hopes of profit. It’s not the first time tech has made the trade against freedom; IBM made it during the Holocaust. In venture capital, you are what you fund. Andreessen and Horowitz understand this, even embody it. But they aren’t just funding the issues they discuss on their podcast; they are funding Trump and Vance. That means those donations are anti-abortion, anti-immigration, and possibly even anti-democracy because that is what the Trump / Vance ticket stands for. These are not subsidiary issues: these are now what two of Silicon Valley’s most prominent figures now stand for, too. Is that a good investment? Correction July 24: An earlier version of this article misstated the donation strategy of a crypto super PAC. The group also spends money on Democratic candidates, not just right-wing ones.

articles.title: JUST NU: Hon sparkas – efter bara fem dagar
articles.summary: För fem dagar sedan utsågs Katie Zacharia till Vita husets presstalesperson. Nu är det dock över, skriver New York Times. – Det här kanske inte är rätt jobb för henne, säger Trump på fredagen.
articles.body_text: För fem dagar sedan utsågs Katie Zacharia till Vita husets presstalesperson. Nu är det dock över, skriver New York Times. – Det här kanske inte är rätt jobb för henne, säger Trump på fredagen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Anthony Scaramucci hade rekordet som den talesperson i Vita huset som suttit kortast tid. Han sparkades av Trump under hans första mandatperiod efter elva dagar på posten. Rekordet innehas nu av Katie Zacharia, 42. New York Times rapporterar att hon har fått sparken. – Jag sa: ”Du borde tänka om, för du vill inte gå igenom det här”, säger Trump. Zacharia har efter sin fiaskoartade debut blivit hårt kritiserad. Zacharia svarade på fredagen med att hon ”gjorde sitt bästa”. Presskonferensen har hånats på sociala medier, bland annat av Joe Bidens tidigare pressekreterare Jen Psaki som skrev på X att den ”i princip var en Saturday night live-sketch”. Trump säger att han pratat med Zacharia, och menar att hon behandlats ”extremt dåligt av medier”. – Jag sa till Katie för bara två minuter sedan, jag sa: ”Katie, du vet, du behöver inte göra det här om du inte vill.” Hon sa att det här är mycket tuffare. Jag sa: ”Välkommen till Trumps värld”. Presidenten menar att han sagt till Zacharia att ”tänka om”.

articles.title: GVFÖ-Agusts nya karriär – ska leda Tranemo
articles.summary: GVFÖ-profilen Agust Örn Monod har blivit politiker. Hans första uppdrag blir i kommunstyrelsen i Tranemo kommun. Det är bara en av flera stora livsförändringar sedan dejtingprogrammet.
articles.body_text: GVFÖ-profilen Agust Örn Monod har blivit politiker. Hans första uppdrag blir i kommunstyrelsen i Tranemo kommun. Det är bara en av flera stora livsförändringar sedan dejtingprogrammet. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Den som såg SVT:s Gift vid första ögonkastet 2023 kommer kanske ihåg det så kallade ”bajspalatset”, det utedass som deltagaren Agust hade utanför sitt egenbyggda hus i Uddebo i Tranemo kommun. Äktenskapet från programmet höll inte och sedan dess han även deltagit i tävlingsprogrammet Robinson. Men nu har han bytt ut realityn mot något annat: kommunpolitik. – Det känns bra att kliva fram, säger han. I årets kommunval stod han som förstanamn på Miljöpartiet i Tranemos valsedel och på fredagen stod det klart att han tar plats i kommunstyrelsen tillsammans med politiker från Socialdemokraterna och Centerpartiet, något som P4 Sjuhärad också har rapporterat om. Han har inte någon lång politisk karriär bakom sig. – Ja, jag börjar som politiker nu kan man säga, skrattar han. Det var en granne som själv är politiskt engagerad som frågade Agust om han ville vara med, något som han till slut nappade på.

articles.title: Kallt – varnar för osynlig is
articles.summary: Trafikverket larmar om osynlig is i Västsverige. Och enligt meteorologen Niklas Einevik har hösten anlänt i stora delar av landet.
articles.body_text: Trafikverket larmar om osynlig is i Västsverige. Och enligt meteorologen Niklas Einevik har hösten anlänt i stora delar av landet – med temperaturer runt nollan. – Men efter helgen byter det väderregim, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I slutet av helgen och på måndag morgon ökar risken för blixthalka i Västsverige, skriver Trafikverket i ett pressmeddelande . Det handlar om så kallad svarthalka – som oftast inte syns men gör vägen extremt hal. Trafikanter i området uppmanas att sänka avståndet och hålla längre avstånd till fordonet framför. Enligt SMHI ser söndag och måndag morgon kyliga på många håll i landet. Det ser däremot inte ut att bli läge för myndigheten att utfärda en vädervarning. – Ingen prognos tyder på ishalka just de dagarna. Men i stora delar av landet har hösten anlänt och går ner mot nära eller strax under noll grader, säger Niklas Einevik, meteorolog SMHI. På lördagen drar ett regnområde in över Stockholmsområdet som sträcker sig ner mot Skåne. Regnet ser ut att lämna Stockholmsområdet och Östergötland under dagen. – Regnet dröjer sig kvar fram på kvällen i ett stråk från Skåne och upp över Blekinge, östra Småland, Öland och Gotland. I de områdena kan det vara ihållande regn under större delen av lördagen. I övrigt ser lördagen ut som en solig dag i stora delar av landet. – Det blir inte jättevarmt utan upp emot sju till åtta grader i söder och i norra Sverige så ligger det på enstaka plusgrader som mest, säger Niklas Einevik.

articles.title: Centerpartiets SD-nej luckras upp i landet
articles.summary: Centerpartiets nej till SD luckras upp runtom i landet – nu bubblar frågan i centerkretsar. I Växjö ska C styra med aktivt stöd av SD.
articles.body_text: Centerpartiets nej till SD luckras upp runtom i landet – nu bubblar frågan i centerkretsar. I Växjö ska C styra med aktivt stöd av SD. – Vi har ingen direktkontakt, de låter Moderaterna föra samtalen med oss, säger Pernilla Wikeland (SD). Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På måndag meddelar talman Andreas Norlén vem som får nästa sonderingsuppdrag. Magdalena Andersson (S) föll i första omröstningen. Hon kan få tillbaka uppdraget, men det kan också gå till Ulf Kristersson (M). En del menar att C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist borde få det. Hur Centerpartiet väljer att agera kan bli avgörande. Om C byter fot om SD kan Kristersson samla en majoritet, och vinna en statsministeromröstning. Matilda Molander, chef för C-närstående tankesmedjan Fores, öppnar i en debattartikel i DI för en lösning hon kallar ”alliansen 3.0”. ” Det kräver att SD utöver att avstå från ministerposter också går med på stora sakpolitiska eftergifter ”, skriver hon bland annat. Samtidigt kunde Expressen avslöja att Centerpartiet i Region Stockholm just nu överväger ett samarbete av den modellen. Michaela Haga, partiets gruppledare i regionen, beskriver det som att C fortsatt söker samarbete i mitten. Hur hon ställer sig till SD-stöd svarar hon inte på.

articles.title: Dissar rödgröna möten: ”Tråkigt”
articles.summary: De fyra rödgröna partierna har bildat ”kartell” för att säkra majoritet i riksdagen. Men C dyker inte upp på gemensamma möten.
articles.body_text: De fyra rödgröna partierna har bildat ”kartell” för att säkra majoritet i riksdagen. Men C dyker inte upp på gemensamma möten. – Det skapar osäkerhet kring vilka som faktiskt utgör riksdagens majoritet, säger V-gruppledaren Samuel Gonzalez Westling. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På torsdagen blev Magdalena Andersson som väntat nedröstad som statsminister. Några regeringsförhandlingar mellan de fyra rödgröna partierna framstår fortfarande som avlägset, eftersom Centerpartiet alltjämt säger nej till Vänsterpartiets krav på ministerposter. Enligt S-ledaren har det dock ”skett framsteg”. Hon pekar till exempel på att de fyra partierna ”bildat kartell”, alltså säkrat majoritet i riksdagens utskott. I praktiken innebär det att man kan göra upp i vissa sakfrågor i väntan på en ny regering. Hittills har man kommit överens om en stopplag mot tonårsutvisningarna och att frysa handelsavtalet med Israel. Men nu har samarbetet i riksdagen börjat knaka i fogarna. Trots att gruppledarna för S, V, C och MP gjort upp väljer Centerpartiet att nobba partiernas gemensamma förmöten, som hålls innan utskotten sammanträder. Istället får S, V och MP göra upp i blindo, och hoppas på stöd från C. ”Just nu vägrar C att ens samordna den löpande sakpolitiken i den riksdagsmajoritet dom varit med och skapat”, skriver Vänsterpartiets vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson på X.

En kvinna beställde pizza från en restaurang genom Foodora. När matbudet kom fram insisterade han på att han skulle bära in pizzan i hennes lägenhet, berättar kvinnan i förhör. Mannen, som är 35 år gammal, följde med henne in och ställde maten i köket. Sedan ska han ha knuffat och tryckt ner henne och sagt ”nu ska vi bara göra detta också”. Därefter våldtog han henne. Kvinnan grät, sa nej och bad honom att sluta. Därefter lämnade matbudet lägenheten och kvinnan kontaktade polis. Enligt egen utsago kom mannen fram till lägenheten sent på natten. Han säger att kvinnan var sur och att hon ska ha spottat på honom. ”Han minns inte om han spottade tillbaka”, står det i domen. Därefter ska han ha torkat sig i ansiktet och åkt hem, enligt egen utsago.

Därefter inleddes en utredning om misstänkt valfusk i Borlänge, där han valdes in. Men han har inte tjänstgjort i riksdagen. På riksmötets öppnande närvarade ledamoten inte.
